q: Logistic regression for 5 classes using one-vs-one trains how many models?
Which loss does logistic regression minimise?
why: Log loss is the negative Bernoulli log-likelihood and is convex for the sigmoid.

q: A coefficient of 0.69 in logistic regression means one unit increase in x…
why: e^0.69 ≈ 2, so the odds multiply by 2.

q: A random forest overfits. Which change does NOT help?
why: More trees only stabilise the average; they don't reduce each tree's overfitting.

q: Roughly what share of rows is out-of-bag for each tree?
Plain bagging differs from Random Forest because bagging…
o: uses all features at every split
why: Random Forest adds random feature subsets per split to decorrelate trees.

q: In XGBoost the optimal leaf weight is:
why: From the second-order expansion with L2 penalty λ on leaf weights.

q: In XGBoost, γ (gamma) is…
why: Splits with gain below γ are pruned.

q: For log loss, min_child_weight limits the minimum sum of…
why: It's the minimum hessian sum in a child; confident rows contribute little.

q: How does XGBoost treat missing values?
o: Learns a default direction per split
why: Sparsity-aware split finding tries both sides and keeps the better one.

q: LightGBM's main growth difference from XGBoost's default:
why: Leaf-wise growth splits the single best leaf; control with num_leaves.

q: GOSS in LightGBM keeps…
o: all large-gradient rows and samples the rest
why: Large gradients are most informative; small ones are sampled and up-weighted.

q: CatBoost avoids target leakage in categorical encoding using:
why: Each row's encoding uses only rows before it in a random permutation.

q: Bagging mainly reduces ___, boosting mainly reduces ___.
why: Averaging decorrelated trees cuts variance; sequential residual fitting cuts bias.

q: An AdaBoost weak learner with 50% error gets weight α =
why: α = ½ ln((1−ε)/ε) = ½ ln 1 = 0.

q: Which models need feature scaling?
why: Distance and margin based models depend on feature magnitudes.

q: Large C in a soft-margin SVM gives…
why: C is the cost per violation; large C fits training points harder.

q: Large γ in an RBF SVM tends to…
why: Each point's influence becomes very local.

q: Training accuracy of 1-nearest-neighbour is usually:
why: Each point's nearest neighbour is itself.

q: The zero-frequency problem in Naive Bayes is fixed by:
why: Add α to every count so no probability is exactly zero.

q: K-means vs KNN:
why: Only the letter k and the use of distances are shared.

q: Why standardise before PCA?
why: Large-unit features would dominate the first component.

q: L1 regularisation tends to:
o: Set some weights exactly to zero
why: The L1 ball's corners lie on the axes, producing sparse solutions.

q: 2% positives. Which metric is most informative?
why: PR-AUC focuses on the positive class; its random baseline is 0.02.

q: When should SMOTE be applied?
why: Otherwise synthetic points leak test information.

q: Missing a fraud costs 9× a false alarm. Cost-optimal threshold (calibrated)?
Gini = 0.5. AUC = ?
why: AUC = (Gini + 1)/2.

q: Top 10 results contain 4 relevant items; there are 8 relevant in total. Precision@10 and recall@10?
Which ranking metric only looks at the first relevant result?
why: Reciprocal rank = 1 / rank of the first relevant item.

q: Correct validation for monthly sales forecasting:
why: Train on the past, validate on the future.

q: Same patient appears in many rows. Use:
why: Keep each group's rows in one fold.

q: PSI of 0.32 on your score suggests:
why: Above 0.25 is a major shift.

q: Smoothed target encoding pulls rare categories toward:
Which error metric is most affected by one huge miss?
why: Squaring makes large errors dominate.

q: Random search beats grid search with the same budget mainly because…
o: it tries more distinct values of each important parameter
why: Only a few parameters matter; the grid wastes trials on the rest.

q: SHAP values for one prediction add up to…
why: Additivity: baseline + Σ φ = prediction.

q: A dense layer from 784 to 128 units has how many parameters?
Stacking 10 linear layers with no activation gives…
o: a model equivalent to one linear layer
why: Products of linear maps are linear.

q: For sigmoid + binary cross-entropy, ∂L/∂z equals:
why: The sigmoid derivative cancels, leaving p − y.

q: Sigmoid's maximum derivative is:
He initialisation sets Var(w) to:
why: ReLU zeroes half the inputs, so twice the Xavier variance.

q: Why can't all weights start at zero?
why: Same output, same gradient, forever.

q: AdamW differs from Adam by…
o: decoupling weight decay from the adaptive update
why: Decay is applied directly to weights, not through the gradient.

q: Inverted dropout with p = 0.5 scales kept activations by:
why: Divide by 1 − p so expected values match inference.

q: LayerNorm computes statistics over…
why: That's why it's batch-size independent.

q: Output size: 32×32 input, 5×5 kernel, no padding, stride 1?
Parameters in a 3×3 conv from 64 to 128 channels:
In an LSTM, the gradient along the cell state is multiplied by:
Your loss turns NaN after a few steps. First thing to try?
why: Exploding updates are the usual cause.

q: Perplexity is…
why: e^CE.

q: Before nn.CrossEntropyLoss you should pass…
why: It applies log-softmax internally.

q: Why divide attention scores by √d_k?
o: To keep softmax from saturating as dimensions grow
why: Dot-product variance grows with d_k.

q: A causal mask prevents a token from attending to…
why: So next-token training can't peek at the answer.

q: Hidden size 768 with 12 heads gives per-head dimension:
GQA mainly reduces…
why: Fewer key/value heads to store.

q: Self-attention cost grows with sequence length n as:
why: n × n score matrix.

q: Which model family is best for producing sentence embeddings and reranking?
why: Bidirectional encoders like BERT.

q: Top-p = 0.9 keeps…
o: the smallest set with cumulative probability ≥ 0.9
why: Nucleus sampling.

q: Temperature below 1 makes the distribution…
why: Logits divided by T < 1 grow apart.

q: LoRA with r = 8 on a 4096 × 4096 matrix trains how many parameters?
Policies change monthly and answers need citations. Best approach?
why: RAG updates by re-indexing and cites sources.

q: RRF with k = 60: a document ranked 1st in one list and absent from the other scores:
Cross-encoders are used for reranking rather than first-stage retrieval because they…
o: need a model call per query-document pair
why: Too slow over millions of documents.

q: Retrieval misses a chunk with the exact product code typed. Add:
why: Keyword search matches exact tokens.

q: Faithfulness measures…
o: share of answer claims supported by retrieved context
why: Groundedness, not correctness.

q: In an agent, who actually executes a tool call?
why: The model only proposes structured calls.

q: DPO differs from RLHF-PPO because it…
o: skips the separate reward model and RL loop
why: Direct loss on chosen vs rejected pairs.

q: Which clause runs first?
why: FROM, then WHERE, then GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

q: Salaries 160, 140, 130, 130, 110. DENSE_RANK of 110?
why: DENSE_RANK has no gaps: 1, 2, 3, 3, 4.
RANK skips after ties: 1, 2, 3, 3, 5.

q: SELECT * FROM t WHERE id NOT IN (1, NULL) returns…
why: id <> NULL is UNKNOWN for every row, so nothing is TRUE.

q: With ORDER BY and no frame, a window's default frame is…
o: ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW
RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW
why: RANGE includes peers (ties), which is why ties share a running total and LAST_VALUE surprises people.

q: A condition on the right table of a LEFT JOIN, placed in WHERE, makes it behave like…
why: Unmatched rows have NULLs on the right and fail the condition. Put it in ON.

q: Best tool for 'users with 3+ consecutive login days' of variable length streaks?
why: The difference is constant within a consecutive run.

q: COUNT(CASE WHEN status='x' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts…
why: COUNT counts non-NULLs; 0 isn't NULL. Use SUM or drop ELSE.

q: 2 requests/s arrive, each takes 5 s. About how many are in progress?
why: Little's law: concurrency = arrival rate × time = 2 × 5.

q: A churn list used by the retention team every Monday should be served by…
why: The decision is made on a schedule, so batch is simplest and cheapest.

q: New model scores every request but users only see the old model's output. That's…
why: Shadow mode: zero user risk, paired comparison on live traffic.

q: PSI of 0.31 on a key feature suggests…
why: Rule of thumb: above 0.25 is a major shift; check the pipeline, then recalibrate or retrain.

q: Best autoscaling signal for a vLLM server?
o: Queue length / time to first token
why: The GPU does the work; scale on what users feel.

q: A semantic cache served last month's numbers for 'sales this month'. The fix?
o: Exclude time-sensitive questions and key by data version
why: Similar wording can mean different things; scope and version the cache.

q: Fraud threshold should mainly be set by…
why: Flag the top k the SIU can review; measure precision/recall at k.

q: Agent run crashed after sending an email; the retry must not resend it. Use…
why: Idempotency keys make retries safe for side effects.
